title: Clean Stock, Quarantine, Sanitation & Movement Control

content.overview: Biosecurity reduces introduction and spread by controlling plant-material entry, clean-stock status, movement between zones, tools/equipment, people, water/root-zone pathways, waste and release authority. No single sanitation step replaces the layered system.

vocabulary.definition: A controlled separation status used while identity, health/testing, risk or release criteria remain unresolved.
Rules that limit how plants, tools, people, water, equipment or waste move between areas of different biosecurity risk.
The designated role permitted to remove a plant/lot/area from a hold or quarantine after required criteria are satisfied.

sections.title: Start with incoming material and stock status
sections.body: Pathogen-tested or otherwise validated clean stock, controlled receiving and separation reduce the chance that disease is amplified through repeated vegetative propagation.

sections.title: Control pathways, not just plants
sections.body: Tools, contact surfaces, water/root-zone pathways, people, waste and movement between rooms can carry biological risk. Design one-way or risk-based workflows and keep clean-to-dirty transitions explicit.

sections.title: Sanitation must be validated locally
sections.body: Research can identify candidate disinfectants or treatments, but operational concentration, contact time, compatibility, worker safety, label/legal requirements and efficacy must be validated for the facility. The course does not prescribe a universal sanitizer recipe.

workedExamples: If a cutting lot has unresolved HLVd status, keep identity and movement restrictions intact while testing is reconciled instead of distributing the lot because plants look healthy.
commonMistakes: Allowing tools to move from suspect to clean areas without the controlled sanitation process.
Letting the person who notices a problem independently release the hold without designated authority.
content.practicalApplication: Draw a facility biosecurity flow from receiving to donor/propagation to vegetative/flower areas. Add controls for tools, people, water, waste and suspect-material escalation.
content.summary: Effective biosecurity is layered and pathway-based. Clean stock, separation, movement control, validated sanitation, traceability and controlled release work together.
